title: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) - GPS L5 (1176 MHz) for WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Ana Reyes

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) filter targeting GPS L5 (1176 MHz) for WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter. The filter is designed on 36° YX LiTaO3 substrate with a target center frequency of 2129.5 MHz and bandwidth of 173.7 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave)
- Frequency Band: GPS L5 (1176 MHz)
- Application: WiFi 6E Coexistence Filter
- Substrate: 36° YX LiTaO3
- Package: SiP (System in Package)
- Design Tool: PathWave EM Design
- Design Center: Osaka Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design targeting GPS L5 (1176 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       2129.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       173.7 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.2 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 22.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 46.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 19.0 dB
Q Factor:               13912
Temperature Coefficient:-22.5 ppm/°C
Die Size:               1.2 x 0.8 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   3
Electrode Material:     Pt/Al
Passivation:            Si3N4
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open PathWave EM Design and load the SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: 36° YX LiTaO3 with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 2129.5 MHz, BW 173.7 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.2 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (SiP (System in Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, 36° YX LiTaO3).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Anritsu MS46122B ShockLine.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 6388 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.2 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 22.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 261 MHz offset >= 46.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 4 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 6.0 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +34 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 98%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-09-09
Devices Tested:         30
Insertion Loss (meas):  0.86 dB
Return Loss (meas):     23.6 dB
Rejection (meas):       49.3 dB
Isolation (meas):       24.0 dB
Q Factor (meas):        13912
Group Delay Variation:  7.4 ns
Power Handling:         +32 dBm
Die Yield:              95.3%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) design demonstrated acceptable performance for GPS L5 (1176 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Cross-talk between adjacent filter channels was below -55 dB.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
